# Sigma-algebra generated by a collection

↑ **Parent:** [Sigma-algebra](sigma-algebra.md)

The [sigma-algebra generated by a collection](sigma-algebra-generated-by-a-collection.md) is the smallest [sigma-algebra](sigma-algebra.md) containing all sets in that collection. The displayed intersection is over a nonempty family, since the power set is one candidate. An intersection of sigma-algebras contains the whole space and is closed under complements and countable unions, proving it is a sigma-algebra and establishing minimality.

For example, the half-lines $(-\infty,x]$ generate the [Borel sigma-algebra](borel-sigma-algebra.md) on the real line. They are Borel, and conversely $(-\infty,b)=\bigcup_n(-\infty,b-1/n]$ and $(a,b)=(-\infty,b)\setminus(-\infty,a]$ recover every open interval. Preimages of these half-lines similarly generate the [sigma-algebra generated by a random variable](sigma-algebra-generated-by-a-random-variable.md).
